notes: Race rules per vehicle class, keyed by the class id in vehicles.json; a class missing here gets generic defaults. Percentages are shares of the lap time. label and color: the class badge in multi-class races. field: default grid size, cars per team, drivers per car (they share the driving in stints) and the spread (standard deviation) of car and driver pace. race: default length, either distanceKm (laps rounded up) or minutes, a time limit, and a standing or rolling start. pace: racePct is how much slower race laps are than qualifying before fuel and tyres (engine modes, tyre saving); consistencyPct the lap-to-lap scatter; overtaking is how readily the class's drivers go for a pass and how late they dare to brake for one (0 = never; bikes: how easily a pass succeeds). fuel: typical kg per km on the reference circuits, tank size, refuelling rate (0 = no refuelling). tyres: compounds with their type (slick, inter or wet), pace offset to the fastest slick, life in km on the reference circuits and pace lost at the end of that life; mustUseTwo requires two different slick compounds in a dry race. A class without an inter or wet compound gets a generic wet tyre. pit: whether stops are allowed at all, stationary time for four tyres, whether refuelling and tyres happen at once, mandatory stops, the shortest stationary time of a mandatory stop, the time a driver change takes (done while refuelling), the longest a driver stays in the car, and repairS: how much longer a stop takes to repair contact damage (a new nose on a single-seater, bodywork on a closed car; this project's own rough figures). drs: the lap from which it is enabled and the gap in seconds at the detection point. air: share of drag removed when right behind another car (within 0.3 s; most of it is gone half a second back), and share of downforce lost in its wake. incidents: a driver's chances per lap of a mistake, a trip off the track and a crash, and technical retirements per 1000 km; in a race of cars part of each comes from contact between cars side by side (see ARCHITECTURE.md, Contact and mistakes). flags: whether race control uses a safety car, and a virtual safety car (vsc, everyone vscPct slower than the race lap) or a full course yellow (fcy, a speed limit of fcyKmh) or neither (null). In a multi-class race the fastest class's flags apply. reference: average wheel energy (MJ/km) and tyre work per km on the real circuits in data/circuits, printed by scripts/raceReference.ts; fuel and tyre wear scale with a track's own values against these. All figures are approximate defaults meant to be edited.
weekendNotes: weekend: the race weekend before the race. practice: sessions with their length in minutes, the day of the weekend they run on (the track loses some rubber overnight) and longRuns where teams run their race simulations. qualifyingDay: the day qualifying runs. qualifying: stages in order, each a session of some minutes with the cars it takes (entry; everyone when missing): the top count of an earlier stage or of practice (from "practice", the best laps over the practice sessions listed, 1-based, or all), the rest after them, or odd or even places (groups); driver picks a crew's driver (0 = the fastest). The grid comes from the last stage a car ran in, later stages in front and groups taking places in turn; with averageTimes from the mean of its best laps over the stages; with knockout the same number of cars goes out at each step whatever the field size, the last stage keeping its size. evolutionPct: how much slower a green track is than one fully rubbered in. redFlag: where cars wait (pitlane: queued at the pit exit; track: stopped in single file before the line), whether the stoppage is added to the race clock, a standing or rolling restart (rollingWhenWet: rolling on a wet track), whether tyres may be changed (work), how many laps back a race that is not resumed is classified, completeAtPct (bikes: a race stopped after this share of its distance is over), whether rain alone stops the race, whether the practice and qualifying clocks stop, and what a car that brings out a red flag in qualifying loses (none, best, best2, all). Figures from the 2026 sporting regulations (2025 for MotoGP and WorldSBK), see weekendSources; the IndyCar groups are split by practice here (in 2026 by the previous race), GT World Challenge runs its three qualifying sessions unsplit (the 2025 format), GT4 qualifying is the session that sets the first race's grid.

stewardsNotes: stewards: what the stewards give a car that is wholly or predominantly to blame for a collision or for forcing another car off the road (collision), and what they give in mitigating circumstances (lesser): a number of seconds, driveThrough, or warning. timeAtStop: a time penalty is stood still in the box before the work of the car's next pit stop, and added to its race time when it makes none (false: always added to the race time). serveLaps: how often the car may cross the line before it comes in for a drive-through (laps under a safety car, a virtual safety car or a full course yellow do not count, and it is not served then); afterLine: the car has to cross the line under green before it comes in. lateLaps, lateMinutes: a drive-through given in the last laps or minutes of the race is not driven, and driveThroughS is added to the race time instead (0: the series sets it per event from the length of the pit lane; here what the pit lane costs at the circuit, to the next five seconds). firstLapLenient: contact on the first lap is judged more leniently. afterRace: incidents are looked at after the race, unless it is completely clear who was at fault. Who is to blame is decided the same way for every series, by the FIA driving standards guidelines (see ARCHITECTURE.md, Stewards). Figures from the regulations and stewards' decisions in stewardsSources, which says where one rests on a single decision or on another series of the same organiser. Bikes have no stewards yet.

stewardsSources.guidelines: FIA Formula 1 Driving Standards Guidelines v4.1 (20 February 2025): https://api.fia.com/sites/default/files/f1_driving_standards_guidelines_version_4.1_feb_20_2025.pdf
stewardsSources.f1: FIA 2026 F1 Sporting Regulations, B1.9 (the penalties and how they are served; 20 s for a drive-through in the last three laps): see weekendSources. The 10 s and 5 s from the FIA's 2025 Formula 1 Penalty and Point Guidelines (14 May 2025): https://www.fia.com/sites/default/files/2025_f1_guidelines_penalty_points_overview_-_14_may_clean_0.pdf. First-lap leniency is stewards' practice, not in either document
stewardsSources.f2: FIA 2026 F2 Sporting Regulations, Article 39 (the same penalties and procedure as Formula 1): see weekendSources. The 10 s from the 2026 decisions at Melbourne and Montreal; the 5 s and the first-lap leniency taken over from Formula 1
stewardsSources.indycar: 2026 IndyCar rulebook, 7.2.3 (black flag penalties, served under green after crossing the line), 9.2.2 and 9.3.3 (avoidable contact): see weekendSources. A drive-through for avoidable contact from the 2026 box scores (Arlington, Sonsio Grand Prix); 30 s for one not served from Road America 2026
stewardsSources.hypercar: 2026 FIA WEC Sporting Regulations, 7.4 (four crossings of the line, not under a neutralisation, the time for an unserved drive-through set per event) and clarification D03 of 3 February 2026 (the last 15 minutes): https://www.fia.com/sites/default/files/wec_2026_d03_all_sporting_clarifications_03022026.pdf. A drive-through for a collision is the practice of the ELMS stewards (same organiser); no WEC decision was looked up
stewardsSources.lmp2: ELMS 2026: decision no. 28 at Imola (a drive-through for a collision) and bulletin no. 1 at Spa (30 s for a drive-through notified in the last 15 minutes): https://elms.alkamelsystems.com. The procedure (four crossings of the line) taken over from the WEC regulations
stewardsSources.gt3: 2026 GT World Challenge Europe Sporting Regulations, Article 15 (time at the next pit stop, two crossings of the line, the last 10 minutes, the time for an unserved drive-through set per event): see weekendSources. A drive-through for causing a collision from the 2026 decisions (Article 27.4)
stewardsSources.gt4: GT4 European Series Sporting Regulations 2026, Article 16.5 (30 s for a drive-through not served) and the 2026 decisions (a drive-through for causing a collision, Article 33.4): https://www.gt4europeanseries.com. The procedure taken over from GT World Challenge Europe (same organiser)
stewardsSources.tcr: 2026 TCR Europe Sporting Regulations, Articles 39 to 41 (a time penalty is added to the race time; three crossings of the line; 30 s in the last three laps; incidents normally investigated after the race): see weekendSources. The 5 s from decision no. 13 at Mugello 2026 (causing a collision)
